questions.question: What is an underpainting?
choices: An initial layer that establishes composition, values, or color relationships
A painting made beneath a frame

questions.question: What is glazing in painting?
choices: Applying a thin transparent layer over a dry layer

questions.question: How does wet-on-wet painting work?
choices: A transparent layer is applied after drying
The paper is painted before it exists
New paint is applied while the underlying paint is still wet

questions.question: What can a dry-brush technique create?
choices: A perfectly smooth wash every time
Broken, textured marks with little paint on the brush

questions.question: Why might an artist use an appropriate ground or primer?
choices: It prepares the surface and can influence adhesion and appearance

questions.question: What is a wash in watercolor?
choices: A broad, relatively transparent layer of diluted pigment
A method of framing a work

questions.question: What does impasto mean?
choices: Paint applied thickly so brushstrokes or texture may remain visible

questions.question: How can an artist create a smooth transition between two colors?
choices: Apply unrelated colors in separate dry dots
Use a ruler to erase the boundary
Blend them gradually while both areas are workable

questions.question: What is a palette used for?
Why should an artist test a mixture before applying it to a large area?
choices: Paint can look different as it dries or across a larger surface
A test guarantees exact color under all light

questions.question: What does layering allow a painter to do?
choices: Build color, depth, and detail through successive applications

questions.question: A watercolor area has a hard edge the artist did not intend. What may have happened?
choices: The brush made a contour drawing
The wash dried before it could be softened

questions.question: Why is brush control important?
choices: It affects edge, mark, coverage, and surface texture
It determines the artwork's historical period
It removes the need to plan

questions.question: What is a resist technique?
choices: A technique that removes every layer
A material blocks paint from adhering to selected areas
A brush made only for outlines

questions.question: How can underpainting support a limited palette?
choices: It guarantees all colors will be bright
It establishes value structure that can guide later color layers
It makes the final layer unnecessary

questions.question: Why might an artist vary brush size?
choices: Every brush creates the same mark
A large brush always creates more detail
Different marks and areas call for different levels of control

questions.question: What should be considered when choosing between acrylic and watercolor?
choices: Opacity, drying behavior, surface, and intended effects

questions.question: What is a highlight in a painted form?
choices: A lighter area that suggests reflected or direct light
A layer applied only at the end

questions.question: A painting feels muddy after many mixtures. What could improve the next attempt?
choices: Use cleaner color mixtures and plan layer relationships
Cover the entire painting in black

questions.question: Why should painting cleanup and ventilation instructions be followed?
choices: They replace the need for drying time
Materials and solvents may require safe handling
